text:
maria: Quick heads-up — while running the onboarding sample-app against staging I hit repeated 429s when paginating embeddings. SDK retries weren't honoring "Retry-After" header. Anyone else seeing this?
kevin: Saw it this morning too. JS SDK uses exponential backoff but ignores Retry-After if header present. Python respects it. Seems like a parity bug.
sam: :facepalm: yep that's the one. JS client uses a generic backoff wrapper and we forgot to check headers. I opened PR #2145 with a fix + unit tests that simulate 429+Retry-After.
julie: Is that also why the sample-runner spikes quota usage? The sample app spins up ~50 concurrent page fetches by default.
maria: Exactly. Two things compounding: (1) the ignored Retry-After so clients keep retrying, (2) sample-app parallel pagination has no backpressure. We should add an adaptive concurrency layer.
kevin: I can add a small RequestQueue to the JS SDK: semaphore-based concurrency + token-bucket rate limiter. Minimal API, opt-in. Something like `new RequestQueue({concurrency: 8, qps: 20})`.
sam: Sketch looks good. Also expose `onRetry` and `retryMetadata` so callers can surface UX messages and metrics. Example: 
```js
const q = new RequestQueue({concurrency:8, qps:20});
await q.enqueue(() => client.listPages({cursor}));
```
julie: dev-bot just deployed sample-app v0.3.1 to staging :white_check_mark: — can we roll the queue into the next staging tag?
dev-bot: deploy: sample-app v0.3.1 -> staging completed (build 8821).
maria: Another pagination note: support resumable pagination using `next_cursor` + checkpointing on disk. Right now the sample app keeps pages in memory and retries everything on failure.
kevin: I'll rework the sample app to stream pages as an async iterator and checkpoint cursors to a temp file. Also add a flag `--concurrency` in the runner.
sam: And we should add a test harness that simulates server 429s with `Retry-After` header and asserts the client waits the right amount and doesn't exceed set QPS. I'll add integration tests to the SDK repo.
julie: Can we also add a short devex doc: "Best practices: throttling, pagination, and backpressure" with copy-paste patterns for JS + Python default configs? New users bump into this during onboarding a lot.
maria: Yes — I'll file a DX ticket to add the doc, update quickstart, and link the sample-app PRs.
sam: Will include telemetry specs: emit `retry_count`, `last_retry_after_ms`, `effective_qps` so Console can show hotspots.
julie: Happy to pair on the async iterator rewrite later today. Ping me when you open the draft PR. :thumbsup:
maria: tagging @kevin @sam to follow up. Thanks all — feels like a small set of changes that should cut quota noise and onboarding friction.
